en: The Noble Dhāraṇī Sūtra of Holding the World,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma, Imperially Appointed Court Rank of Chao San Dafu, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, under Imperial Edict.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Lokadhara addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
if there should be anyone who receives, maintains, reads, and recites this dhāraṇī..."
"How should one receive and uphold [this teaching]? We pray that the Buddha will expound it.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Dhāraṇīdhara, saying:
"If there should be another person..."
On the first day of the bright fortnight of the second month,
he entered the water at that river which flows alone into the sea.
Once the water has reached the milk, stand facing east toward the sun with palms joined,
reciting and upholding this mantra from the moment the sun rises until it sets.
Having emerged from the water,
one shall abstain from food for seven days,
reciting and upholding [the mantra] day and night without speaking with anyone.
Thereafter, one should paint the actual form of Dhṛtarāṣṭra;
when about to apply the colors,
one should do so with a mind of precious devotion.
Anoint silk with sandalwood water from a white *candana* tree and let it remain for one night as an offering of sincere devotion.
He commanded the master painters to observe the fast and precepts,
bathe, don new clothes,
and give rise to a heart of profound reverence.
Adorn it with colors according to the ritual rules;
the image shall be ten cubits in height and three cubits in width.
The color is deep green.
Seated upon a lotus flower,
he is adorned with immeasurable splendor.
The colors are brilliant and pure;
its radiance is like that of the sun.
In the right hand, it holds a fruit.
His left hand is in a gesture of consolation;
his countenance is serene and joyful;
before his seat is a dragon king.
Holding in their hands precious caskets, true jewels, jeweled vases, coral, agate, gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and various other kinds of treasures,
they made offerings with pure hearts,
placing the various devas upon them.
There is a net of jewel-cloud rain;
on the right side, Mahāśrīdevī holds a lotus flower and offers consolation,
while Śrīratnapāṇi stands in attendance on the left side.
His physical form is perfectly complete, his body adorned with necklaces;
he holds a lotus flower in his hands in a gesture of reassurance.
An image of Dhṛtarāṣṭra should be placed in the location of the śarīra.
One should offer arghya water, various kinds of fine foods, flower garlands, clarified butter, and lamps;
furthermore, one should repeatedly provide offerings of exquisite flowers, clarified butter, incense, lamps, food, and drink to Pināka and the Yoginīs.
May there be no demonic interference.
Having extended these offerings,
he further offered immeasurable quantities of sandalwood, aloeswood, and agallochum, as well as various exquisite incenses, ghee, and oil lamps.
Facing the visualized image of the Bodhisattva,
focus the mind with single-minded devotion,
sit upright, and recite the mantra.
Beginning from the hour of the Tiger (寅時),
one enters the maṇḍala;
this may last for seven days, or two weeks, or even as little as a single day.
"At the time of sunrise, may all your aspirations be fully accomplished.
Then the World-Honored One addressed Jaganmṛdha, saying:
"Furthermore, if there should be a person..."
Furthermore, entering into the water at midnight and reciting this dhāraṇī eight hundred times,
one shall obtain the fulfillment of all wishes within that same month.
The Buddha told Jie-shi (Jagatīdhara):
If there is another person who,
at midnight, recites and upholds the name of the Bodhisattva Lokeśvara according to the rite,
having purified themselves in accordance with the dharma.
Within six months,
one will certainly obtain what is desired.
Thus spoke the Buddha to Dhāraṇīdhara.
Furthermore, if there is a person who hides wealth and property,
and later forgets it.
If one recites and maintains this according to the Dharma,
one will certainly obtain wealth and goods.
Thus spoke the Buddha to Jie Shi.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who desires to seek a position of honor and rank,
they should enter the water during the day and recite and maintain this mantra.
At midnight, one again performs homa using sesame seeds;
for every single seed, there is one recitation and one burning,
continuing until eight hundred repetitions are reached.
One will certainly obtain great joy, wealth, honor, and fulfillment.
The Buddha told Jie Shi:
"Furthermore, if there is another person..."
Mix white mustard seeds with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Recite the mantra once for each seed and burn them one by one.
Perform the *homa* ritual according to the procedure previously described.
The king obtained joy and celebration,
and the land was free from calamity.
The Buddha told Dhṛtarāṣṭra:
Furthermore, if there is a person who uses exquisite milky incense mixed with clarified butter (ghṛta) to perform homa,
following the ritual procedures as previously described.
It can pacify all calamities and misfortunes of great ministers.
The Buddha told Dhāraṇīdhara:
"Furthermore, if there should be another person..."
In the middle of the night,
with a sincere mind, recite and uphold the name of the Bodhisattva,
maintaining purity according to the Dharma.
Within seven days, one will obtain great wealth, joy, and the fulfillment of accomplishments.
The Buddha told Dharaṇīdhara:
"Furthermore, if there is another person..."
Begin the ritual on the first day of the waxing moon.
Observe the fast and precepts,
and install an image of a Bodhisattva at the site of the śarīra.
Make offerings according to the Dharma,
recite and uphold the names of the Bodhisattvas,
and make aspirations with a sincere mind.
He will surely manifest a transformed body before them to offer consolation,
so that they attain non-retrogression.
They give rise to the bodhisattva practice.
The Buddha told Dhāraṇīdhara:
"Furthermore, if there is another person..."
Maintaining a vegetarian diet and pure conduct,
abstaining from meat and wine,
they constantly recite [the scriptures] day and night.
One shall attain great wealth and nobility.
At that time, the World-Honored One proclaimed this ritual manual as the "Root Mantra.
He then spoke the mantra within the assembly, saying:
*Namo ratnatrayāya oṃ vasudhāri svāhā | oṃ laukikami-bhūtalā ni-vāsinyai svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this mantra, [remained silent].
He addressed Jie-shi, saying:
"All seal-dharmas (mudrā) serve to represent mental dharmas;
they are also called 'external manifestations'."
When forming this mudrā,
join the two hands in the hollow of the palms; then,
extend the index fingers while keeping the fists closed in between.
The ring fingers are held upright;
the little fingers are interlaced as in the *kṛti* mudrā;
and the middle fingers are straight, their shape like needles.
The forms and characteristics of these seals abide in those eight directions,
each separated from the others;
this is the seal of the ritual procedure for Sustaining the World (Lokadhara).
By forming mudrās and reciting the vidyā-mantra according to the ritual,
all aspirations will be accomplished and one will extensively benefit sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
Oṃ śrīye śrī-kāritāna kāritānye kārisvāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One...
Having spoken this mantra,
he addressed Jaganmohana, saying:
"This is the seal of samādhi."
One should first join the palms together,
using the thumbs to bend them inward into the palms.
This is called the Seal of the Samādhi that Sustains the World.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
Oṃ samaye svāhaye samayakari mahāsamaye svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Jaganmātṛ, saying:
The mantra for this samādhi seal is as follows.
Furthermore, when applying it in the world,
one should use the index finger and bend the third joint of the middle finger.
With the thumb extended upward,
this mudrā is called the fundamental mudrā of the Bodhisattva Lokeśvara;
it is used for summoning the noble ones and sages.
When escorting the sages and worthies,
one should perform this mudrā in all cases.
Thus spoke the Buddha to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
Apply it by extending the head outward horizontally;
this is called the Flower Seal (puṣpamudrā).
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the mantra, saying:
"Oṃ vāsudhe svāhā. The Buddha told Dharaṇīṃdhara:
"One should receive and uphold this flower-seal mantra in this manner.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Dharaṇīṃdhara.
If there is another person who should extend their middle fingers horizontally,
this is called the Incense Seal (Gandha-mudrā).
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
Oṃ vasudhāri svāhā. Having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One [concluded].
He addressed Jie-shi, saying:
"Furthermore, if there is a person who extends their ring finger outward,"
This is called the Ointment Incense Seal (*vilepanamudrā*).
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
*Oṃ vasumatiśrīye svāhā*. When the World-Honored One had finished speaking this mantra, [he said:]
He addressed Jie Shi, saying:
"If there is another person who wishes to perform this,
they should use the little finger and the thumb to pinch together and form it."
The remaining three fingers are extended like a three-pronged vajra;
this is called the lamp mudrā.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
Oṃ vasudhārāṇi svāhā. At that time, having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One addressed Lokadhara, saying:
"Furthermore, if there should be a person..."
The application of the two hands is like the motion of scooping water.
Cross the thumbs over so that they pass outside the index fingers.
This is called the *āhāra-mudrā* (Food Seal).
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
Oṃ dhāraṇi dhāraṇi svāhā. Having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One [ceased].
He addressed Jaganmātṛ, saying:
"All other offerings are identical to the root mudrā;
they are to be consecrated by the mantra."
If one uses it for ordinary purposes,
one should empower it with the constant mantra and seal.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to paint an image of the Bodhisattva Dharaṇīdhara,
they should use fine, new silk that is exquisite and without flaw.
According to the measurement of a Buddha-cubit,
it should be two chi in length and one chi in width.
Upon the image, a Buddha is installed;
on the right side is an image of the Holy Avalokiteśvara,
and on the left side is established an image of Vajrapāṇi.
Between the Buddhas, place an image of Lokeśvara.
The form of the image is golden in color;
the Bodhisattva’s right hand performs the mudrā of granting boons (*varada-mudrā*).
Adorned with various kinds of pearls, lapis lazuli, and even agate, all used as ornaments;
on the lower right side, place the practitioner who recites and maintains [the mantra],
bowing his head with his right hand in prostration.
Holding a crown in the left hand,
one should depict the Bodhisattva within a white lunar month and recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.
They made offerings according to their capacity.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Jie-shi, saying:
"Furthermore, suppose there is a person who wishes to cultivate a field."
The person who recites and maintains [this mantra] shall bathe, put on new clothes,
observe the fast and precepts,
and place an image of a Bodhisattva within the field.
Furthermore, one should offer ointments, flower garlands, necklaces, and exquisite, precious food and drink as offerings.
One should recite the name of the Bodhisattva up to eight hundred times.
Additionally, before the image, one should consecrate scented water.
Recite [the mantra] eight hundred times.
Fill the "Wise Vase" (bhadraghaṭa) to the brim and place it before the image.
Have the field-dwellers, the oxen, and the plowshares stand in a row.
One should then sprinkle it with water from the vessel of the worthy (bhadraghaṭa).
It is the same for the person who recites and maintains [the mantra] as they sprinkle it;
one should have that person circumambulate this field as well as those people and cattle.
After circumambulating seven times,
one may then sow the seeds.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Jaganmṛgāra, saying:
Furthermore, if there is someone who intends to harvest a field,
they should establish the Saṃgha at the four corners of the land and provide them with food and drink according to the Dharma.
The practitioner who recites and maintains this [mantra] shall bathe, wear clean garments,
observe the fast and precepts,
and further place a sacred image within the field.
Furthermore, one should again present various offerings of flowers, incense, lamps, candles, food, and drink.
One should recite the mantra to empower them for eight hundred times.
Then, before the image, one should place a flask filled with scented water.
Recite [the mantra] eight hundred times and further empower it.
Install the image of the Bodhisattva facing east.
By making offerings with pure hearts— using scented ointments, clarified butter, flower garlands, food, and drink—
the grains and fruits will increase manifold,
and all calamities and misfortunes will be eliminated.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, saying:
"Furthermore, if there were a person who,
regarding this heap of grain..."
In the four intermediate corners, place four young maidens wearing fresh,
clean garments; they shall observe the fast by consuming only vegetarian food.
If one recites and maintains this dhāraṇī while empowering it,
the grain will increase and calamities shall not invade.
Furthermore, Holder of the World,
when measuring grain,
that person should bring to mind the honorable title of the Bodhisattva.
If the person reciting and upholding [the mantra] does not produce sound,
but recites silently with single-minded devotion,
the measure will increase even further once it is completed.
The Buddha told Jie-shi:
"Furthermore, suppose there is a person whose fields have first ripened."
One should first make offerings to the Buddha and the noble assembly;
this increases merit immeasurably and beyond all praise.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Jaganmṛdha, saying:
Furthermore, if there is a person who,
at the time of storing [grain],
first paints two short figures inside the granary.
Naked and with a large belly,
he holds a wicker basket in his hands and makes the gesture of pouring out grain.
The grain was golden in appearance.
Within this granary, various items were arranged;
thereafter, many kinds of exquisite incense were burned inside the granary.
Along with various flowers,
*argha* water, incense, parasols, banners, and all manner of offerings,
he further placed the Bodhisattva inside the granary.
Furthermore, sprinkle cow’s milk inside the granary while reciting the mantra,
and remove all other items.
When entering wealth and grain,
there will be auspiciousness and no calamities.
Furthermore, World-Upholder:
In this treasury, one should arrange fresh food and offer incense and flowers as an offering,
while receiving, upholding, and reciting this dhāraṇī.
They shall be free from all calamities.
Furthermore, Holder of the World,
if there should be another person...
Furthermore, by using colored silk to transcribe the *Jie shi tuoluo ni jing* (Upāśikā Dhāraṇī Sūtra),
and by incensing it, reciting it, and upholding it with reverence,
one’s merit will increase immeasurably.
It pacifies and eliminates calamities.
The Buddha told Jie-shi (Dharaṇīdhara):
"If a person recites and upholds it..."
One should first purify the mind and recite this dhāraṇī eight hundred times.
By reciting it three times each day,
one's aspirations will surely be fulfilled.
The Bodhisattvas bestow their grace.
Furthermore, Holder of the World,
if there should be another person...
To fulfill all one's aspirations,
one should fashion an image of the Holy Bodhisattva Lokapāla in the northeast corner of one's own dwelling.
Using exquisite colored silks, one should depict [the image] according to the ritual rules.
Upon completion of the work, it should be installed in a clean place.
With a sincere mind, one should make offerings of *argha* water, unguents, incense, sandalwood, aloeswood, and various other fragrances.
Furthermore, one should employ the five precious gems, the five medicinal herbs, and even the five grains.
Cover the neck of the *argha* vessel with silk;
do not open this vessel.
By reciting and upholding this dhāraṇī according to the ritual,
all one's aspirations shall be completely fulfilled,
and one's wealth and possessions will increase.
They shall obtain immeasurable merit.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Dhāraṇīdhara.
If there are sentient beings who wish to construct a storehouse,
according to its size, whether large or small,
when they wish to take [from it]—
One should offer food mixed with ghee as an offering to the honored image.
Recite this dhāraṇī one hundred and twenty times according to the ritual;
once this number is fully reached, [the rite is complete].
Only then did he emerge,
having stilled and eliminated all calamities.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Jie-shi (Dhṛtarāṣṭra), saying:
Furthermore, if there is a person who has gone far away with their wealth,
and their kinsmen and bones are filled with anxiety and distress,
they should take white *śāka* grass and plant material, wash them to extract the juice.
Mix cow bezoar, saffron, camphor, sandalwood, and musk with *argha* water.
Draw [the deity] upon a ship and,
with a pure mind, recite and maintain this *dhāraṇī*.
Wealth and goods shall arrive swiftly;
distant journeys shall be safe and auspicious;
may all increase and be fulfilled.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra, saying:
*Tadyathā | jile jile agaca agaca vagavadati*. When the World-Honored One had finished speaking this mantra, [he continued].
He further addressed Lokadhara:
"If anyone should receive and uphold this dhāraṇī,
they will be able to fulfill all the aspirations of sentient beings."
It is like the element of water pervading the earth;
it is like the sunlight that can dispel all darkness;
and it is like the moonlight that brings coolness to things.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
*Tadyathā | dhānanu varuṇa śrīṃvā indra śrīṃvā sudṛḍhasa*.

"This mantra is named the *Hṛdaya-dhāraṇī* of the Bodhisattva Jagatīdhara."
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, with a pure mind, receives and upholds this dhāraṇī,
remembering it without forgetting,
they will be able to extinguish grave offenses.
One shall obtain immeasurable merit,
abandon the three evil realms,
and perfect wealth and nobility.
All their aspirations were fulfilled without exception,
until they ultimately attained the unsurpassed fruit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Lokadhara and the assembly of noble ones—
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were filled with immeasurable joy;
they prostrated themselves at his feet and, with faith and acceptance, put it into practice.
*The Holy Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Upholding the World*.
